faq.q: What do I do when the product photo still shows the room?
faq.a: Upload it and download a file where the product sits on white. On a teapot, the handle and the lid knob both stay inside the frame.

faq.q: How can I create white-background product photos?
faq.a: Make them in the tool: upload a photo, run the white-background job, and download the finished file.

faq.q: Does a marketplace main image have to sit on white?
faq.a: Often it does, and a grey-looking field is a common reason a listing image gets sent back. Open the current rule for your category before you publish, and read the [plain main image guide](page:guide-white-background-amazon) when the store is Amazon.

faq.q: Can the product look like a paper cutout on white?
faq.a: It can, if the source photo is flatly lit and the base has no weight. On a boot, the shadow under the sole makes it read as standing on the page.

faq.q: Does a white product photo cost anything?
faq.a: Yes. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. One photo spends 24 credits. Those credits also pay for videos.

faq.q: Can I apply a white background to many product photos?
faq.a: Yes. Send the folder through the API, or click through the files in the app.

faq.q: How many credits does one photo use?
faq.a: One product photo uses 24 credits. You see that number before the job starts. If the photo fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: What should the starting photo show?
faq.a: The whole product, with edges that are not cut off. A simple setting in the original photo makes the white result easier to check.

faq.q: Can I post the file on Amazon, Shopify, or Etsy?
faq.a: Yes. The download has nothing stamped on it, and you can use it in the shop and in ads.

more_sections.h2: Where Your White Background Photo Goes Next
more_sections.lead: The finished file can go on the product page, and the folder behind it can follow when you are ready.

items.t: The File on the Product Page
items.d: The saved kettle file can go live on the Shopify product page you are editing. If a marketplace feed reads images from that page, it picks up the same file.
Your catalog software can request the white field through the API, so a new photo does not wait for someone to open it by hand.
Ten new jar photos can take the same white field in one run inside the app. You are not standing up a queue of your own.

items.t: When the Catalog Outgrows a Plan
items.d: A larger month can keep the same white field when Premium is not enough. You say how many photos you make, and that run uses the same field.

more_sections.lead: The same account also builds, fixes, and exports the other images a listing needs. White is one job. The cards below are the rest.

items.d: The plant comes off the patterned rug and sits by itself. That pot is ready for the field the listing asks for next.
The toaster can sit on a walnut desk while the metal color stays the one in your photo. You get a new setting without a new shoot.

items.t: Place It in a Room Scene
items.d: A buyer choosing a throw can see it on a sofa, not only as a folded square. That second image is there when the listing needs context.
A lantern photo that came out dim can be brightened before the store grid gets its square. The shade no longer hides the bulb.
The linen shirt can appear worn, with the stripe spacing from your photo kept. That avatar stands in, so the Thursday fitting does not have to happen.
The file you save has no mark across it, so you can attach it straight to the product page you are editing.
The gold hoop keeps its shape while the blown highlight on the metal comes down. The earring looks like metal again, ready for the listing.
A tall photo of a phone case can fill a wide ad frame. The camera cutout stays in the picture while the white field grows out to the sides.

items.t: Use the API From Your Shop
items.d: The shop's product tool can call the API when a new SKU is saved. The white field is requested from the tool you already use.
The scent name can sit under the candle in the font the site already uses. The story image goes up with the name already on it.

items.t: One Square for a Whole Folder
items.d: Twelve spoon photos can all become the same square in one run. The set matches in the grid without resizing each file by hand.

items.t: A Note Left for a Teammate
items.d: The person who writes the product title can leave a note on the crop and save the next version in this same account. The listing does not stall in someone's inbox.
The next banner can pull a wordmark you saved once, instead of a second version typed in a different weight.

items.t: A Logo for a New Line
items.d: A spice line can get a simple logo from one sentence about the tin and the shop name. Place that mark on the label area and the line looks finished.

items.t: The Same Login on Every Device
items.d: The phone in the stock room uses the same login, so the scarf file the desktop job just finished is already there. You can approve it between boxes.

reasons.h2: Who Uses a White Background Maker
reasons.lead: A single listing and a full catalog both end with one product, alone on white. Shoppers can compare the item without the room behind it.

items.d: The soap dispenser beside the sink becomes a main image with the counter gone. The pump and the base stay in the frame, so you can list from the photo you already took.
A folder of this week's new SKUs can get the white field without anyone opening each file. Point the API at that folder and move on to the next listing.
New arrivals get the same white field, margin, and shadow as last season's products, so a growing catalog still reads as one set.
